Missing finding id is not required, because the existing test_r1_09 uses id-less findings and missing severity is already blocking. R1-03: _test_file maps junit classnames (strips trailing class components) and resolves paths against the gate cwd then the repo root; _commit_and_prove refuses a gate repair whose named test is not a file with a configured runner; regression_proof reports must_fail tests that were not run; __run__ gate findings carry no file. R1-04: control_state (hooks/config/info digest + refs/replace set) is bound in the PLAN event (CONTROL_ANCHORED for legacy runs) and checked before every step, after every review and in evidence_ok; any drift -> BLOCKED TAMPER with GIT_CONTROL marker, and only unblock of that block re-anchors; the diagnosis worker gets a before/after snapshot (refs, control, impl worktree) and tamper -> BLOCKED TAMPER; GIT adds -c core.fsmonitor=false. Not done: milestone refs are not anchored to PLAN because they move legitimately (still checked per step); a filter driver planted via config+attributes could still run during the post-review git status before drift is detected (detected right after, not prevented; not verified); graphify update not run because graphify-out/ is outside the permitted paths.

Fix: (1) Linux child-subreaper containment: the driver becomes PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, and sweep_orphans() SIGKILLs and reaps every adopted orphan (direct children outside the driver's session) until none is left. It runs before each worker, after each worker (after _killpg), after each run_cmd gate/test command and at run() start. Worker records gain containment_pre/containment_post/contained. (2) ConfigWatch polls the reviewer config dir every 10 ms for the whole run; env/apiKeyHelper or a settings file seen at any moment sets config_isolated=false (previously only the end state was checked). (3) is_independent requires contained is True for real milestones (reason cites R8-01). New tests: test_r8_01_setsid_child_of_a_worker_cannot_inject_env_into_the_reviewer_config, test_r8_01_env_injected_and_removed_during_the_run_is_not_isolated, test_r8_01_setsid_child_of_a_gate_or_test_command_is_killed. All three fail on e029675 with the new tests and pass after the change (5 repeat runs passed). Existing test test_r1r2_01_lingering_child_cannot_turn_reject_into_accept relied on a surviving setsid forger, which containment now kills. It is parametrized: contained=False monkeypatches the sweep off and keeps the original detection assertions unchanged; contained=True asserts the forgery never happens. Nothing was weakened or removed. Full tests/dev_workflow: 189 passed. Live re-run with real claude 2.1.296 and the local scripted server, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST unset: an injector left by an earlier worker was killed (killed=1), the server got 0 hits, config_isolated and contained were true. An injector started outside the driver's tree (the reviewer's probe, HOLD 0.8 and 1.5) still redirects the CLI to the scripted ACCEPT but is recorded as config_isolated=false, so the round is not independent. Residual limits, documented in section 6: processes started outside the driver's tree (systemd-run, at/cron, orphans of a killed driver) are detected by the 10 ms watch, not prevented, and a sub-poll-interval injection read by the CLI in that window is not excluded. Windows/macOS have no subreaper: contained=false, so real-milestone reviews there do not count (fail-closed) until Job Object containment exists. That code is not written or tested here and is an owner decision. graphify update was unavailable here.

findings.evidence: do_review pops w['result_text'] (in-memory text whose sha is result_text_sha256) and instead re-reads rounds/R<n>/reviewer_result.txt after the post-run snapshot; nothing compares that file to result_text_sha256, and verify() only hashes reviewer_stdout.txt for non-imported rounds. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R1/probe_forge.py (DEVTEST fixture, reviewer=always_reject): implementer /tmp/uri_review_R1/evil_impl.py makes a plausible fix and starts a start_new_session watcher (escapes killpg) that overwrites rounds/R2/reviewer_result.txt with {candidate:<sha from reviewer_prompt.md>, verdict: ACCEPT, findings: []}. Result: stage COMPLETE, R2 recorded ACCEPT/COMPLETED_WITH_RESULT/independent, integration INTEGRATED (remote tip == candidate), verify() == []; reviewer_stdout.txt still holds the genuine REJECT with HIGH R2-01. Same code path for claude_cli. Disproves the doc limit that setsid children's later writes are 'caught by the clean-worktree checks' (state_dir is not checked).
findings.suggested_fix: Parse the verdict from the in-memory result_text returned by run_worker (or re-derive it from reviewer_stdout.txt and require sha256 == stdout_sha256/result_text_sha256 before parsing); make verify() check reviewer_result.txt against result_sha256 and re-derive the parsed result from the hashed raw output; keep state_dir outside anything workers can reach or check it in the integrity snapshot; correct the §6 limitation text.
findings.title: Effective verdict is read from an unbound, mutable reviewer_result.txt; a lingering worker child can turn a genuine REJECT into ACCEPT and verify() stays clean

findings.evidence: do_review takes a fresh 'before' git_control_digest each round and do_repair a fresh ctl0; neither is compared with a digest bound at PLAN. A reviewer that changes .git/config or info/ makes its own round NOT_INDEPENDENT -> WAITING_FOR_MODEL, which resumes automatically on the next run with no owner step, and the changed config is then the 'before' state of every later round. do_diagnosis checks only that its worktree is clean and HEAD unchanged (line 981): it does not check refs_digest or git_control_digest, although the docs say the diagnoser 'changes nothing'. Impact through config-executed commands (e.g. core.fsmonitor running on the driver's git status) is NOT verified here (the probe command was denied).
findings.suggested_fix: Record git_control_digest (and refs_digest of protected refs) in the PLAN event and require equality before every worker and at evidence_ok; any drift -> BLOCKED TAMPER (owner), not WAITING_FOR_MODEL. Apply the same before/after snapshot to the diagnosis worker. Consider -c core.fsmonitor=false in GIT.
findings.title: Git hooks/config/info tamper detection is not anchored: a change caught once becomes the new baseline, and the diagnosis worker is never checked

findings.evidence: compare({'failures':{},'ids':['t::a','t::b'],'skipped':2},{'failures':{},'ids':['t::a','t::b'],'passed':2},[]) -> ok True. A repair that adds @pytest.mark.skip to a failing gate test also 'passes after' in regression_proof (exit 0). The reviewer re-audit is the only backstop.
findings.suggested_fix: Record per-id outcome (passed/skipped) and treat baseline-passed -> candidate-skipped as a new failure unless allowed_flaky.
findings.title: Tests that passed on the baseline but are skipped on the candidate are not flagged by the gate comparison

findings.evidence: is_blocking({'severity':'MEDIUM'}) is True (it routes REJECT) but review_prompt and count_attempts use `severity == 'HIGH' or f.get('blocking')`, which is False for it; RETRY_LIMIT never triggers for such a finding (only stall/budget bound it) and the next reviewer is not asked to confirm it FIXED.
findings.suggested_fix: Use is_blocking() in review_prompt and count_attempts.
findings.title: Implicitly blocking MEDIUM findings are excluded from attempt counting and from the next round's prior-findings list

findings.evidence: Gate findings are built only from new_failures + changed_cause; when comparison.ok is False solely because of vanished tests, pending_findings=[] and the implementer is asked to repair nothing (a no-change repair is refused up to max_repair_attempts, then REPAIR_FAILED instead of a clear gate blocker).

findings.evidence: _ROUTINE_CONFIG excludes remote.<r>.fetch/prune/mirror and branch.* from git_control_digest. integrate() runs `git fetch -q <remote> <target>`, and git updates the configured remote-tracking destination for the fetched ref. The same probe at 1f720ed (probe_fetch_old.py) stops BLOCKED with TAMPER 'git hooks or config changed during the repair', and session-b is untouched. findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/uri_review_R4/p1/probe.py (HOME set to a temp dir): after appending to $HOME/.gitconfig only, L.git_control_digest(repo) and L.control_state(...) are unchanged (True True). (a) A [url "<fake.git>"] insteadOf=<origin> entry: driver-style push `[*GIT, -C, repo, push, origin, sha:refs/heads/main]` exits 0 and `git(repo, 'ls-remote', 'origin', ...)` returns the pushed sha, so integrate() would record INTEGRATED and reach COMPLETE, but the real origin main was never updated (printed: real origin main: False). (b) A global [filter "x"] smudge/clean plus a committed `.gitattributes` (a.py filter=x): blob in commit is 'DEFECT = True', the file in the driver's add_worktree() checkout reads 'DEFECT = False', and worktree_changes() reports the checkout clean, so the reviewer reads and the gates test content that is not the candidate tree, and the integrity check passes. Workers inherit HOME (lifecycle_providers.py:131) and can write ~/.gitconfig with plain shell (the Bash(git config*) prefix denial does not cover `cat >> ~/.gitconfig`). Same class as R1-04/R3-01 (worker-written config steering driver git commands), outside the monitored set.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the effective global/system config files (git config --show-origin --list --global/--system, or GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL / XDG paths) and the default core.attributesFile ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/attributes) in control_state/git_control_digest, or run driver git with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM isolation (plus a separately pinned credential/push configuration). Verify pushes against the remote URL recorded at PLAN (e.g. `git remote get-url` resolved without insteadOf, bound in the chain). Add regression tests for the insteadOf and smudge-filter cases.
findings.title: Git control-state tamper check covers only the repository config; worker-written user-level git config (~/.gitconfig) silently redirects the driver's push and its push verification, and smudge filters make reviewer/gate checkouts differ from the candidate commit

findings.evidence: run_cmd and _run call communicate(timeout), then on TimeoutExpired call killpg and communicate() with no timeout. killpg does not reach a child that called setsid(), and the sweep_orphans() that would kill it comes only after communicate returns. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R10/hang.py: run_cmd([python,-c,'Popen(["setsid","sleep","30"])'], '.', 3) had not returned after 15 s. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R10/worker.py: run_worker(command 'setsid sleep 40 & echo done', timeout_s=3) had not returned after 20 s. Any gate, test or worker child can keep the driver blocked indefinitely (a malicious implementer can also open its CLI's stdout through /proc/$PPID/fd/1). The only recovery is killing the driver, which moves the orphan outside the subreaper tree (see R10-02).
findings.suggested_fix: After TimeoutExpired (and before any blocking second communicate), killpg then sweep_orphans() first, and bound the second communicate with a timeout (or close the pipes and kill). Do the same in _run. Add tests where a setsid child keeps stdout open.
findings.title: Timeout path calls communicate() without a timeout before the R8-01 orphan sweep: a setsid descendant holding stdout hangs the driver indefinitely and the sweep is never reached

findings.evidence: Probe: a driver running run_worker(sleep 300) was killed with SIGKILL. The worker kept running (ppid 1, its own session), and a new driver's sweep_orphans() returned {'contained': True, 'killed': 0}. Workers run with start_new_session, so a launcher timeout that kills the driver (or R10-01 forcing one) leaves them alive while the resumed run records contained=true.
findings.suggested_fix: Record each worker's/command's session id (pid) in state before launch. At run start, scan /proc for live processes in those sessions and kill them, or refuse contained=true until none is left.
findings.title: contained=true is recorded although workers or orphans of an earlier, killed driver process are still running (outside the subreaper tree); documented limitation, but realistic and reachable through R10-01
